_comment2: Orisia meets the full party at the Army Camp. She assigns personal sidequests
_comment3: to each recruited member. Flood's sidequest check has a special branch.
_comment4: The scene ends with the point-of-no-return confirmation prompt.

speaker: Orisia
text: So. This is the party that's been making noise across every region between here and the capital. I expected more of you — or less. It's hard to say.

speaker: Orisia
text: My name is Orisia. I command what's left of the Third Accord's forward force. We've been holding this position for eleven days. That ends when you and I finish this conversation.

speaker: Orisia
text: Before we move, I want to know who I'm marching with. Each of you — I have something that needs doing. Consider it a test. Consider it preparation. Consider it whatever helps you sleep.

_comment2: Each block is only shown if the character is in the party.

speaker: Orisia
text: Michael. You know the roads. I need you to map the three supply corridors east of camp and mark any blocked passages. We're blind out there and that has to change before tomorrow.

speaker: Michael
text: Give me a blank chart and three hours. I'll have something usable.

speaker: Orisia
text: Cookie. My soldiers haven't had a proper meal in four days. Whatever you can do with what's in the camp stores — do it. Morale is a weapon and ours is running low.

speaker: Cookie
text: Four days? That's... I'll see what I can manage. Don't expect miracles. Expect stew.

speaker: Orisia
text: Iris. We have wounded who haven't been properly treated. I need assessments — who can walk, who can fight, who can't. Be honest with them. They'll respect that more than false comfort.

speaker: Iris
text: I'll start at the east tent. How many are we talking?

speaker: Orisia
text: Thirty-two. Maybe thirty-three. We stopped counting after the sixth day.

speaker: Orisia
text: Yipp. You've been studying the infection. I need a written summary — something my officers can read without a scholarly background. Simple. Actionable. What spreads it, what slows it, what we can do in the field.

speaker: Yipp
text: I — yes. Yes, I can do that. I've been meaning to write a condensed version anyway. I'll have it ready before we march.

speaker: Orisia
text: Fritzzit. And Crankpot, I assume you go where he goes — I need the camp's siege equipment inspected. Half of it has been sitting in the rain for a week and I need to know what still fires straight.

speaker: Fritzzit
text: Oh, now this is a language I understand. Come on, Crankpot — let's see how badly they've been treating these beautiful machines.

speaker: Orisia
text: Frostbite. I don't know exactly what you are or what you can do — and that means the enemy doesn't either. I need you at the northern perimeter. Show yourself just enough to make them uncertain.

speaker: Frostbite
text: Uncertainty. I can do uncertainty.

_comment: Special Flood branch: if all other sidequests are assigned (or characters absent),
_comment2: Orisia delivers her line about Flood's power before checking if Flood is present.

speaker: Orisia
text: And Flood.

speaker: Orisia
text: She's already as powerful as she will ever be.

speaker: Orisia
text: I have nothing to assign her that she isn't already doing simply by being here.

speaker: Orisia
text: Flood. You'll be our anchor when things go sideways — and they will go sideways. Stay close to the main column. If the line breaks, you hold it.

speaker: Flood
text: Understood.

speaker: Orisia
text: That's everyone. When you're all ready, we move.

speaker: Orisia
text: I'll say this plainly: once we march, there is no coming back to this camp. The supply lines will be cut to prevent pursuit. Anyone who isn't with us when the order goes out will be left behind.

speaker: Orisia
text: Are you ready? You cannot return.

prompt: This is the point of no return.

speaker: Orisia
text: Then we march at dawn.

speaker: Orisia
text: Then take the time you need. But don't take too long — the longer we wait, the more ground we lose.
